title: Getting around
goal: Ask for and give directions, take buses, trains and auto-rickshaws, and tell people what to do (politely or casually).
intro:
Indian streets are lively and street signs are rare, so you'll be asking for directions a lot — and people love to help. This unit gives you places in town, transport and direction words.

The grammar is the **imperative** — the command form. Hindi has three levels to match आप, तुम and तू: **बैठिए** (polite), **बैठो** (familiar), **बैठ** (intimate). Learn the आप form first; you'll use it with every stranger, driver and shopkeeper.

grammar.title: The imperative: telling people what to do
grammar.body:
Match the command to the 'you' you're using:

**आप** (polite): stem + **-इए** *-iye*: बैठिए, आइए, बोलिए, जाइए, रुकिए
**तुम** (familiar): stem + **-ओ** *-o*: बैठो, आओ, बोलो, जाओ, रुको
**तू** (intimate): bare stem: बैठ, आ, बोल, जा, रुक

A few common verbs are irregular in the polite form:
करना → **कीजिए** (करो) · देना → **दीजिए** (दो) · लेना → **लीजिए** (लो) · पीना → **पीजिए** (पियो)

**Don't**: put **मत** before the verb (or the softer **न**) — in speech it often follows the verb instead (डरो मत!): मत जाओ 'don't go', यहाँ मत रुकिए 'please don't stop here'.

The bare infinitive is also used as a mild instruction, a bit like 'remember to…': सीधे जाना 'go straight (then)'. And adding **ज़रा** 'just' softens any request: ज़रा रुकिए 'hang on a sec, please'.

examples.en: Turn right at the next junction (then).

grammar.title: Going places: destination, direction, distance
grammar.body:
With verbs of motion like **जाना** and **आना**, the destination usually needs **no postposition**: मैं बाज़ार जा रहा हूँ 'I'm going to the market'; वह दिल्ली आई 'she came to Delhi'. (You may hear को added, but it's not needed.)

Other useful patterns:
**X से** 'from X' (also 'via / at' a junction): स्टेशन से, चौराहे से दाएँ
**X तक** 'up to, as far as X': पुल तक सीधे जाइए
**X की तरफ़** 'towards X': मंदिर की तरफ़
**X से दूर / X के पास** 'far from / near X'
**X से Y तक** 'from X to Y'

Remember the oblique: चौराहा → चौराहे से, रास्ता → रास्ते में 'on the way'.

dialogue.title: Taking an auto
dialogue.setting: Julia wants to go from her hotel to the Red Fort in Delhi. She waves down an auto-rickshaw.

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.en: Will you go to the Red Fort?

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.en: Yes, I'll go. Two hundred rupees.

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.native: दो सौ? बहुत ज़्यादा है। मीटर से चलिए।
lines.roman: do sau? bahut zyādā hai. mīṭar se chaliye.
lines.en: Two hundred? That's too much. Please go by the meter.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: मीटर ख़राब है, मैडम। चलो, डेढ़ सौ।
lines.roman: mīṭar xarāb hai, maiḍam. chalo, ḍeṛh sau.
lines.en: The meter's broken, madam. OK, a hundred and fifty.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: ज़्यादा दूर नहीं। बीस मिनट लगेंगे, अगर ट्रैफ़िक कम हुआ।
lines.roman: zyādā dūr nahīṃ. bīs minaṭ lageṃge, agar ṭraifik kam huā.
lines.en: Not too far. It'll take twenty minutes, if there's not much traffic.

lines.speaker: Driver
lines.native: डरिए मत, मैडम। वह देखिए — सामने लाल क़िला है।
lines.roman: ḍariye mat, maiḍam. vah dekhiye — sāmne Lāl Qilā hai.
lines.en: Don't worry, madam. Look — there's the Red Fort in front of us.

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.native: बहुत बढ़िया! यहीं रोकिए। यह लीजिए, डेढ़ सौ।
lines.roman: bahut baṛhiyā! yahīṃ rokiye. yah lījiye, ḍeṛh sau.
lines.en: Great! Stop right here. Here you are, a hundred and fifty.

culture: Auto-rickshaw drivers are addressed as **भैया** and the classic opening is a question: **X चलोगे?** 'will you go to X?' — agree the fare (or the meter) before getting in. App cabs have made this easier in big cities. Directions are given by **landmarks** rather than street names: 'turn left after the temple, near the big tree'. People rarely say 'I don't know' — if you get a vague answer, ask two or three people. In metros, the first carriage is reserved for women, and on buses some seats are marked महिला 'ladies'.

tip.title: Please …: the -इए form
tip.body:
- To ask politely, add **-इए** to the verb stem: बताना → **बताइए** 'please tell', जाना → **जाइए**, आना → **आइए**.
- With friends use **-ओ**: बताओ, जाओ, आओ.
- A few are irregular: करना → **कीजिए**, देना → **दीजिए**, लेना → **लीजिए**.
- **ज़रा** 'just' makes any request softer: ज़रा बताइए.

tip.title: से, तक, की तरफ़ — at, as far as, towards
tip.body:
- Going *to* a place needs no postposition: मैं बाज़ार जा रहा हूँ.
- **से** 'from / at' a turning: चौराहे **से** दाएँ. **तक** 'as far as': पुल **तक** सीधे.
- **की तरफ़** 'towards': मंदिर **की तरफ़**.
- 'To the right / left / straight on' = **दाएँ / बाएँ / सीधे**. Before से and तक, चौराहा becomes **चौराहे**.
tip.pattern: X से दाएँ  ·  X तक सीधे  ·  X की तरफ़

tip.title: Near and far
tip.body:
- **X से दूर** 'far from X' · **X के नज़दीक** 'near X' (like X के पास).
- Ask **कितनी दूर है?** 'how far is it?'
- Answer in time: **पैदल बीस मिनट** '20 minutes on foot', or **दस मिनट लगते हैं** 'it takes ten minutes'.

lessons.title: Buses and trains

tip.title: Getting on, getting off
tip.body:
- Going **to** a place: no postposition — यह बस बाज़ार जाती है.
- Get **on**: बस **में** चढ़ना. Get **off**: बस **से** उतरना; get off **at** X: X **पर** उतरना.
- 'By bus / by train': बस **से**, ट्रेन **से**.
- बस, ट्रेन and गाड़ी are feminine: बस **जाती** है, ट्रेन **आती** है.

lessons.title: Taking an auto or a taxi

tip.title: Talking to drivers
tip.body:
- Call a driver **भैया** and ask **स्टेशन चलोगे?** 'will you go to the station?'
- With friends, commands end in **-ओ**: रुको, चलो. Politely, **-इए**: रुकिए, चलिए.
- 'Don't': **मत** before the verb — यहाँ **मत** रुकिए.
- रुकना = to stop yourself; **रोकना** = to stop something: गाड़ी रोकिए.

sentences.en: Will you go to the airport? (to a driver)
